qs.q: A patient living in an endemic region presents with massive, chronic secondary lymphoedema of the lower extremities characterized by brawny induration and thickening of the skin. Which of the following is the most common worldwide cause of this condition?
qs.e: Filariasis is parasitic obstruction of the lymphatic channels and is the most common worldwide cause of massive secondary lymphoedema. Chronic lymphatic blockage leads to increased hydrostatic pressure, ECM deposition, and brawny skin induration.
